facts.text: The Terminators is unrelated to the Terminator franchise. The Asylum released it April 28, 2009, three weeks before Terminator Salvation hit theaters on May 21.
The film's first press came February 16, 2009, when /Film's Peter Sciretta posted it under the headline "LOL" as a Terminator Salvation knock-off. No trailer existed yet.
Wikipedia lists the budget of The Asylum's The Terminators at just $250,000. Terminator Salvation went on to gross about $370 million worldwide.
Asylum co-founder David Latt told Vice that a typical Asylum film gets about 3 weeks of prep, 2 weeks of shooting and 8 weeks of post. That's roughly four months from storyboards to store shelves.
Paul Logan plays every single TR-4 android in the film, so the army of identical killer robots is one actor. He's a black belt in Okinawan Go-Ju-Ryu karate.
Asylum co-founder and Terminators writer David Latt told Vice his studio is "a cash-flow company" and that its films "have never lost money." Pay for crews? "Oh, we don't pay anybody."
Around the 11-minute mark, the BMO (Bank of Montreal) building and the base of the CN Tower show up as the cities fall. That's Toronto, standing in for the apocalypse.
Dread Central's Foywonder called the film's big city-destruction effect underwhelming: "a tiny explosion" that looked like a missile hitting one random building, with less smoke than 9/11.
The Asylum shot the film in Los Angeles-area spots like Oxnard and Santa Clarita, plus its own studio. Toronto footage was used for the skyline.
The pistols the TR-4 androids carry are the Auto-9 from RoboCop (1987), the same gun design Peter Weller's Murphy used.
The Shameless Pile blog warned that the DVD cover "lies": it promises a squad of exoskeleton cyborgs, but the movie only has one. Still, the blogger found it "surprisingly fun."
Dread Central reported in February 2009 that the film was due on DVD April 28 and speculated that Warner Bros. and Halcyon, who made Terminator Salvation, might sue over the title and artwork.
A footnote in Dread Central's review says The Asylum pulled the film from its website after a cease-and-desist, then released it anyway. The reviewer called it second-hand.
Months before this film, Fox fired a cease-and-desist letter at The Asylum over The Day the Earth Stopped, a copy of its Keanu Reeves remake. Dread Central noted it in November 2008.
Dread Central's The Foywonder gave it 3 of 5, calling it 'more entertaining than it has any right to be' and livelier than many Terminator copycats. He credited Paul Logan's cyborg performance.
Star A Martinez (Sheriff Reed Carpenter) won a daytime Emmy as Cruz on the soap Santa Barbara. He later led AMC's Longmire and Dark Winds.
Star A Martinez (Sheriff Reed Carpenter) has been acting since The Cowboys (1972). He also played lawyer Daniel Morales on L.A. Law from 1990 to 1994.
Jeremy London (Kurt Ross) is the twin brother of actor Jason London. He played Joey Lauren Adams' ex in Mallrats while Jason played her boyfriend in Dazed and Confused.
Jeremy London (Kurt Ross) joined Fox's Party of Five in 1995 as Griffin Holbrook. He later played minister Chandler Hampton on 7th Heaven, and directed the 2013 horror film The Devil's Dozen.
Director Xavier S. Puslowski also helmed Asylum titles including Mega Shark vs. Giant Octopus (2009), 2012: Doomsday (2008) and Death Racers (2008).
Terminator Salvation, the film this one chased, cost about $200 million. It opened at number two with $42.6 million, the first Terminator film not to debut at number one.
Wikipedia credits the screenplay to Asylum co-founder David Michael Latt, who also co-produced with David Rimawi and Paul Bales. Mark Atkins shot it.
Terminator Salvation's set went viral when star Christian Bale's tirade at cinematographer Shane Hurlbut leaked. Bale had cursed him out for walking onto a set mid-scene.
The Asylum was founded in 1997 by David Latt, David Rimawi and Sherri Strain. Rimawi and Strain came from Village Roadshow Pictures.
The Shameless Pile blog noticed one space commando in this film is named Hicks, the name of Michael Biehn's marine in Aliens. Biehn also starred in the real The Terminator (1984).
IMDb notes the film's story resembles 1973's Westworld and the 2004 Battlestar Galactica reboot more than the 1984 Terminator, despite the title.
Co-star Lauren Walsh (Chloe) also appeared in the 2008 spoof Meet the Spartans.
Sara Tomko (Pallas) later played alien Asta Twelvetrees in the Syfy comedy Resident Alien.
Terminator Salvation recreated Arnold Schwarzenegger's face with CGI from a scan of a 1984 face mold, since he was California's governor. The Asylum just used Paul Logan.
Paul Logan is also known for Asylum's Mega Piranha and for playing Glen Reiber on the soap Days of Our Lives.
Roger Ebert gave Terminator Salvation two stars out of four, summing it up as "Guy dies, finds himself resurrected, meets others, fights." It holds 33% on Rotten Tomatoes.
The film was referenced in Ilsa, the Wicked Warden (2014) and in The Terminator 1991 Remake (2013).
Studio executives cut Terminator Salvation to PG-13, which fans criticized. An R-rated director's cut came later on Blu-ray, while this Asylum film simply went out Not Rated.
The Asylum's biggest hit came in 2013 with Sharknado, about sharks lifted from the ocean by a waterspout and dropped on Los Angeles.
The Asylum's TV ties grew from Blockbuster rentals to Syfy, and later to Pluto TV and Tubi streaming deals.
